sectorLine: Industrials — Optical fibre & devices, wiring harnesses, power cable
headlineHtml: The optical segment is carrying the group: a 30% Infocommunications margin against a 3% harness margin, and a guide that needs H2 to be bigger than H1
ledeLeadHtml: Sumitomo Electric is a five-segment industrial conglomerate — Automotive (wiring harnesses, 57% of sales), Environment & Energy (power cable), Infocommunications (optical fibre, connectors and devices), Electronics, and Industrial Materials & Others (cemented-carbide tools) — whose profit centre has abruptly rotated from harnesses to data-centre optics.
ledeHtml: In FY3/2026 net sales were ¥5,110,171mn, operating profit ¥418,173mn (8.2%), ordinary profit ¥431,274mn and owners' net income ¥369,508mn (EPS ¥473.78 pre-split; ¥118.44 post-split equivalent) — net income flattered by ¥98,149mn of extraordinary income, including a ¥79,154mn gain on sale of shares of subsidiaries and associates. FY3/2027 guidance has been raised twice, to sales ¥5,750,000mn / OP ¥500,000mn / owners' NI ¥370,000mn (30 October 2026). Strengths: (1) Infocommunications is a genuine AI-infrastructure franchise — FY3/2026 OP ¥77,435mn at a 24.6% margin, then H1 FY3/2027 OP of ¥61.2bn at 30.4% (+177% YoY) on fibre, high-density connectors/MT ferrules, fusion splicers and optical devices (EML chips, CW lasers for CPO/NPO, InP substrates), with device/InP capacity planned to ~4.5× the 2024 level by 2028 (company DC strategy deck, 12 November 2026); (2) the whole P&L is inflecting — OP margin 3.6% (FY3/2022) → 8.2% (FY3/2026), guide 8.7% (calculated), mid-term plan 10.0% by FY3/2028; (3) Automotive profit has been rebuilt from ¥12,264mn (0.7%, FY3/2022) to ¥179,700mn (6.1%, FY3/2026); (4) balance-sheet repair is real — interest-bearing debt down from ¥891,680mn (FY3/2023) to ¥557,266mn, pre-tax ROIC 14.7% in FY3/2026 (company, vs 9.3%); (5) two guidance raises in FY3/2027 already, with the dividend raised to ¥44 post-split (¥176 pre-split equivalent); (6) breadth of the DC portfolio across every distance class — submarine fibre (incl. a claimed first multi-core submarine project order), inter-building ultra-high-count cable, intra-DC connectors and devices. Weaknesses: (1) the guide is heavily H2-loaded — H1 delivered 43.9% of guided OP (calculated), so H2 needs ¥280.4bn (+28% vs H1), and Infocommunications alone must print ¥94.8bn in H2 against ¥61.2bn in H1, with no disclosed order backlog to underwrite it; (2) the largest business is the weakest — Automotive OP fell 17.7% in H1 on +17.3% sales (3.3% margin) on Middle East volume loss and copper costs, and the pass-through lag is undisclosed; (3) cash conversion broke in H1 — operating cash flow halved to ¥139.4bn as inventories rose ¥201.7bn to ¥1,219.8bn despite record OP; (4) FY3/2026 net income quality — ¥79,154mn of the PBT came from selling affiliate shares, so the 'record' NI is not an operating run-rate; (5) disclosure gaps are material for a ¥5.1tn-sales company — no regional sales or profit in the tanshin at all (register S4), no orders/backlog, no DC revenue figure despite a 14-page DC strategy deck, and no Q&A at interim briefings (slides only); (6) the stock de-rated violently into the print (¥1,413 on 16 November, −6.98% on the day, ~62% below the June 2026 high on a split-adjusted basis per secondary data) — the market is pricing the optical cycle, not the plan. Rating and price target are Under Review placeholders (see Basis of preparation).

bullets.html: FY3/2027 guidance: initial (12 May 2026) sales ¥5,300,000mn / OP ¥425,000mn → Rev.1 (31 July) ¥5,400,000mn / ¥450,000mn → Rev.2 (30 October) ¥5,750,000mn / OP ¥500,000mn / ordinary ¥515,000mn / NI ¥370,000mn, dividend raised to ¥44 post-split. But H1 OP of ¥219.6bn is only 43.9% of the guide (calculated): H2 must deliver ¥280.4bn, +28% half-on-half, in a company whose H2 skew is normally modest.

H1 FY3/2027: Infocommunications sales ¥201.5bn (+48.8%), OP ¥61.2bn (+177.4%) at a 30.4% margin (calculated) — 28% of group OP on 7% of sales. The supplementary full-year segment forecast is ¥156.0bn of OP, implying ¥94.8bn in H2 alone. Whether a 30% margin is a structural device-mix level or a fibre-shortage peak is the central valuation question; the company discloses neither the price/volume split nor a backlog.

H1 Automotive sales rose 17.3% to ¥1,616.6bn but OP fell 17.7% to ¥53.8bn (3.3% margin vs 4.7%). Disclosed H1 group drags: Middle East situation −¥14.0bn, R&D/depreciation −¥8.0bn, and the Sumitomo Densetsu deconsolidation (now Semlinks) −¥8.6bn (briefing materials). Copper pass-through lag — the segment's largest cost variable — is not quantified. The FY3/2026 recovery to a 6.1% margin is not yet proven durable.

H1 operating cash flow was ¥139.4bn, down 44.7% YoY, while OP rose 43.5%: inventories absorbed ¥201.7bn (to ¥1,219.8bn). The mid-term plan's pre-tax ROIC ≥15% target (FY3/2026 actual 14.7%, company) is incompatible with this conversion rate persisting — how much of the build is optical pre-build vs automotive is undisclosed (pack Q7).

bullets.leadHtml: The plan triples the optical field by FY2028
bullets.html: Mid-term plan (company plan, to the year ending March 2029): sales ¥6,000bn, OP ¥600bn (10.0%), pre-tax ROIC ≥15%, ROE ≥13%. The Infocommunications field — renamed 'Digital & AI' in the May 2026 plan — carries a FY2028 target of ¥970bn sales / ¥240bn OP (DC deck), roughly a tripling of the FY3/2026 segment sales base. No DC revenue ¥ figure is disclosed anywhere in the materials read.

blocks.heading: 1. Key indicators and financial history
blocks.html: Exhibit 1 (page 1) summarises ten fiscal years, FY3/2017–FY3/2026, all J-GAAP as originally reported. The decade divides into a long margin fade and a sharp two-year repair. OP peaked at ¥173,139mn (5.6%) in FY3/2018, slid to ¥113,926mn (3.9%) by FY3/2021 and ¥122,195mn (3.6%) in FY3/2022, then climbed every year to ¥418,173mn (8.2%) in FY3/2026 — sales nearly doubling across the window to ¥5,110,171mn. Owners' net income tracks the same arc (¥56,344mn in FY3/2021 → ¥369,508mn in FY3/2026), though FY3/2026 includes ¥98,149mn of extraordinary income (a ¥79,154mn gain on sale of shares of subsidiaries and associates, ¥10,360mn of fixed-asset sale gains and ¥8,635mn of securities gains, per the FY2026 tanshin) against ¥24,264mn of extraordinary losses — the operating story is the OP line, not the NI line. Operating cash flow was positive in all ten years but volatile (¥76,002mn in FY3/2022 against ¥425,192mn in FY3/2026). Per-share figures cross a break: a 4-for-1 split took effect on 1 July 2026 (register S6); Exhibit 1 EPS is pre-split as reported in each year's tanshin, and FY3/2026 EPS of ¥473.78 equals ¥118.44 post-split (Finnhub's annual EPS agrees).

blocks.heading: 2. Latest update — H1 FY3/2027 results and the second guidance raise
blocks.html: Q2 FY3/2027 results were published on 30 October 2026; the President's briefing slides and a data-centre growth-strategy deck followed on 12 November 2026. The company published slides only — it publishes Q&A summaries only for full-year briefings, so no Q&A record exists for this event (pack source note).

blocks.heading: H1 FY3/2027 results
blocks.html: H1 (April–September 2026) set first-half records at every line (company): sales ¥2,764.9bn (+16.5%), OP ¥219.6bn (+43.5%; 7.9% margin vs 6.4%), ordinary profit ¥231.2bn (+48.7%), owners' net profit ¥159.4bn (+62.7%). Disclosed OP drags within the beat: Middle East situation −¥14.0bn, R&D/depreciation −¥8.0bn, deconsolidation of Sumitomo Densetsu (now Semlinks) −¥8.6bn (briefing materials). Segments (tanshin note, incl. intersegment sales): Infocommunications ¥201.5bn / ¥61.2bn (30.4%); Automotive ¥1,616.6bn / ¥53.8bn (3.3%, OP −17.7%); Environment & Energy ¥546.5bn / ¥33.2bn (6.1%, OP −3.6%); Electronics ¥233.4bn / ¥28.6bn (12.2%); Industrial Materials & Others ¥241.1bn / ¥42.7bn (17.7%, OP +230.7% — cemented-carbide tools on tungsten prices, with three price increases in calendar 2026 per press coverage of the president). Cash: operating cash flow ¥139.4bn (−44.7% YoY); inventories ¥1,219.8bn (+¥201.7bn vs March 2026).

blocks.heading: Guidance chain (Exhibit 3)
blocks.html: Initial (12 May 2026): sales ¥5,300,000mn, OP ¥425,000mn, owners' NI ¥320,000mn. Revision 1 (31 July 2026, Q1 tanshin): sales ¥5,400,000mn, OP ¥450,000mn, NI ¥340,000mn. Revision 2 (30 October 2026, Q2 tanshin): sales ¥5,750,000mn, OP ¥500,000mn, ordinary profit ¥515,000mn, NI ¥370,000mn; dividend raised to ¥44 post-split (interim ¥19, year-end ¥25; ¥176 pre-split equivalent). No explicit company-stated reason for the latest revision was extracted from the tanshin text checked (tracker) — the company published slides only. The arithmetic is demanding: H1 OP progress is 43.9% (calculated), implying H2 OP of ¥280.4bn (+28% vs H1); the supplementary materials' Infocommunications full-year OP forecast of ¥156.0bn implies ¥94.8bn in H2 (vs ¥61.2bn in H1). FX and segment assumptions beyond the Info OP figure are 未取得 in the sources read.

blocks.heading: 3. Business description
blocks.html: Sumitomo Electric Industries (founded 1897; headquartered in Kitahama, Osaka) is the Sumitomo group's electric-wire and materials house. President is Osamu Inoue. It reports five segments (segment profit = operating profit; register S3). The mix is unusually barbelled: a very large, low-margin automotive harness business (Sumitomo Wiring Systems) and a small, now very high-margin optical business, with power cable, electronic materials and carbide tools between them. A 4-for-1 stock split took effect on 1 July 2026.

blocks.heading: Automotive
blocks.html:
Wiring harnesses, connectors and in-vehicle electronics, centred on Sumitomo Wiring Systems. FY3/2026 sales ¥2,935,389mn (57% of group), OP ¥179,700mn (6.1%) — rebuilt from ¥12,264mn (0.7%) in FY3/2022 through price revisions and cost work. H1 FY3/2027 reversed the trend (OP −17.7% at a 3.3% margin) on Middle East volume loss and copper costs; the copper pass-through lag is the segment's key undisclosed variable.

The H1 reversal has named, quantified causes. The group's H1 operating-profit bridge carried three disclosed drags — the Middle East situation at −¥14.0bn, R&D and depreciation at −¥8.0bn, and the deconsolidation of Sumitomo Densetsu (now Semlinks) at −¥8.6bn (briefing materials, 12 November 2026) — and Automotive absorbed the volume and copper side of that bridge: segment sales rose 17.3% to ¥1,616.6bn while operating profit fell 17.7% to ¥53.8bn, taking the margin from 4.7% to 3.3%. Set against the full-year history, the FY3/2026 margin of 6.1% (¥179,700mn) was itself the peak of a rebuild from 0.7% in FY3/2022 (¥12,264mn) built on price revisions and cost work, so the H1 print tests whether that rebuild was structural or a price-revision cycle that copper has now overtaken; the contractual copper pass-through lag, the variable that would settle the question, is not disclosed.

blocks.heading: Infocommunications
blocks.html:
Optical fibre and cable (incl. Pure Silica Core submarine fibre and mass-produced multi-core fibre), ultra-high-fibre-count cable, high-density connectors and MT ferrules, fusion splicers, and optical devices — EML chips, CW lasers for silicon photonics/CPO-NPO, tunable lasers — plus InP/GaAs substrates. FY3/2026 sales ¥315,030mn, OP ¥77,435mn (24.6%); H1 FY3/2027 OP ¥61.2bn at 30.4%. The DC strategy deck (12 November 2026) frames CPO/NPO adoption from 2027 and capacity for intra-DC optical devices and InP substrates reaching ~4.5× the 2024 level by 2028 (7× including non-DC). No DC revenue figure is disclosed.

The data-centre portfolio is specified by distance in the company's 12 November 2026 growth-strategy deck. For submarine and inter-data-centre links it offers Pure Silica Core fibre and mass-produced multi-core fibre — including a claimed first multi-core submarine project order for petabit-class transmission — and ultra-high-fibre-count cable; inside the data centre, high-density optical connector products and MT ferrules, fusion splicers, and optical devices (EML chips, CW lasers for silicon photonics and CPO/NPO, and tunable lasers) on InP/GaAs substrates. The deck frames first-generation CPO/NPO adoption from 2027, the CW-laser share of intra-DC laser-chip demand rising from 47% in 2024 to 73% plus a further 8% high-power CW share by 2028 (company estimates on LightCounting data), and production capacity for intra-DC optical devices and InP substrates reaching about 4.5× the 2024 level by 2028, or 7× including non-DC applications. No data-centre revenue figure is disclosed at any point in the deck; the segment's ¥315,030mn of FY3/2026 sales remain the only hard proxy.

blocks.heading: Environment & Energy, Electronics, Industrial Materials & Others
blocks.html:
Environment & Energy (power cable, magnet wire, energy systems): FY3/2026 sales ¥1,142,598mn, OP ¥90,615mn (7.9%) — margin rebuilt from 5.4% (FY3/2022). Electronics (flexible printed circuits, fine polymer, heat-shrink tubing): ¥350,638mn / ¥39,528mn (11.3%). Industrial Materials & Others (cemented-carbide tools — Sumitomo Electric Hardmetal — sintered parts, A.L.M.T.): ¥366,516mn / ¥31,399mn (8.6%), with H1 FY3/2027 OP +230.7% on tungsten price pass-through (three price rises in 2026, president via press).

Industrial Materials & Others was the group's third-largest profit pool in H1 FY3/2027 and its fastest-growing: operating profit rose 230.7% year on year to ¥42.7bn on sales of ¥241.1bn, a 17.7% margin, against a full-year FY3/2026 margin of 8.6% (¥31,399mn). The report's H1 account attributes the step-up to tungsten price pass-through — three price rises during 2026, per the president via press reports — across the cemented-carbide tool business (Sumitomo Electric Hardmetal) and sintered parts. How much of the H1 pool is semiconductor-related demand and how much is price pass-through that reverses with the tungsten price is not decomposed in the company's materials, and the segment's history argues for care: its operating profit fell from ¥28,193mn in FY3/2019 to ¥6,660mn in FY3/2021 before recovering, the widest swing of any segment in the history block.

blocks.heading: 4. Market and value chain
blocks.html: Sumitomo Electric's value chain runs from materials (glass preforms, InP/GaAs substrates, carbide powders) through components (fibre, connectors, devices, harnesses) to systems (submarine cable projects). Its competitive sets differ by segment: optical fibre/cable against Corning, Furukawa/Lightera, YOFC and Prysmian in a documented fibre shortage; optical devices against Lumentum, Coherent and domestic peers into the CPO/NPO transition the company dates from 2027; harnesses against Yazaki and Furukawa Electric in a structurally low-margin, copper-linked business; submarine cable against Prysmian, Nexans and NKT. The strategic question the print poses is capital allocation across the barbell: the DC deck's ~4.5× device-capacity expansion and the FY2028 Digital & AI target (¥970bn sales) imply capital following optics, while 57% of sales remain in harnesses at a 3–6% margin.

blocks.heading: 5. Segments and regions
blocks.html: Segment profit is operating profit; the disclosed adjustment (mainly unrealised-profit eliminations) is small (−¥504mn in FY3/2026). IMPORTANT — sheet correction: the PL/segment sheet's main-block segment rows for FY3/2022–23 were found positionally mislabelled in the programme audit and corrected in place on 17 November 2026 (register S15; 48 cells); this report uses the corrected copy (see Basis). Regional sales and profit are NOT disclosed in the tanshin in any main-window year (register S4) — the Regions block of the sheet is intentionally empty; regional disclosure exists only in the history block (FY3/2017–19) and in securities-report/briefing materials outside the sheet.

blocks.heading: Segments (Exhibit 2)
blocks.html: FY3/2026: Automotive ¥2,935,389mn / ¥179,700mn (6.1%); Environment & Energy ¥1,142,598mn / ¥90,615mn (7.9%); Infocommunications ¥315,030mn / ¥77,435mn (24.6%); Electronics ¥350,638mn / ¥39,528mn (11.3%); Industrial Materials & Others ¥366,516mn / ¥31,399mn (8.6%). The five-year rotation is the story: in FY3/2022 Automotive earned ¥12,264mn (0.7%) and Infocommunications ¥23,398mn (9.9%); by FY3/2026 Automotive had recovered to ¥179,700mn while Infocommunications' margin had reached 24.6% — and H1 FY3/2027 then pushed Info to 30.4% while Automotive fell back to 3.3%. On the history block (same five-segment basis), FY3/2017 was Automotive ¥1,511,739mn / ¥98,616mn (6.5%), E&E ¥607,494mn / ¥20,807mn, Info ¥196,173mn / ¥21,509mn, Electronics ¥235,981mn / −¥10,898mn (loss), IM&O ¥263,096mn / ¥20,491mn.

blocks.heading: Regions
blocks.html: Not disclosed in the tanshin for FY3/2022–26 (register S4) — no regional sales or profit figures are presented for the main window, and none are estimated here. For the history years the tanshin did disclose regions (register S12): entity-location FY3/2019 sales were Japan ¥1,429,905mn / Asia ¥883,786mn / Americas ¥538,216mn / Europe & other ¥326,078mn, with entity-location OP of Japan ¥81,981mn, Asia ¥79,179mn, Americas ¥15,098mn and Europe & other −¥9,729mn; customer-location FY3/2019 sales included China ¥516,347mn and the USA ¥409,579mn. These bases are historical only and are not spliced into the main window.

blocks.heading: 6. Financial statements summary
blocks.html: FY3/2026 (J-GAAP): sales ¥5,110,171mn, gross profit ¥1,034,031mn (20.2% — the best of the window), SG&A ¥615,858mn (12.1%), OP ¥418,173mn. Net non-operating income of ¥13,101mn gave ordinary profit of ¥431,274mn; extraordinary income ¥98,149mn (affiliate-share sale gain ¥79,154mn; fixed-asset gains ¥10,360mn; securities gains ¥8,635mn) less extraordinary losses ¥24,264mn gave PBT of ¥505,159mn; a low 20.6% effective tax rate and NCI of ¥31,638mn left owners' net income of ¥369,508mn, EPS ¥473.78 pre-split on 779.9mn basic shares (no dilutive securities; register S6). Operating cash flow ¥425,192mn; capex ¥222,228mn; D&A ¥209,842mn. Balance sheet at FY3/2026-end: cash ¥235,921mn; interest-bearing debt ¥557,266mn (register S5 definition, current portion of bonds excluded per the programme's BS-fix note) — net debt ¥321,345mn (calculated), down from ¥612,248mn at FY3/2023-end (calculated); receivables ¥932,945mn; inventories ¥1,018,148mn (2.91 months of cost of sales, PL calculation); payables ¥487,654mn. Company-reported pre-tax ROIC was 14.7% (FY3/2026 MD&A, vs 9.3% in FY3/2025), helped by inventory and cross-shareholding compression. R&D and employees are not presented in the tanshin (register S7).

blocks.heading: 7. Strategy and mid-term plan
blocks.html: The mid-term plan (company plan, through the year ending March 2029) targets sales of ¥6,000bn, OP of ¥600bn (a 10.0% margin), pre-tax ROIC of at least 15% and ROE of at least 13%. The growth engine is explicit: the Infocommunications field, renamed 'Digital & AI' in the May 2026 plan, is targeted at ¥970bn of sales and ¥240bn of OP in FY2028 (DC strategy deck, 12 November 2026) — roughly triple the FY3/2026 Infocommunications sales base, on a renamed-field basis whose exact perimeter versus the current segment is a flagged open question (pack Q10). Supporting moves: optical-device and InP-substrate capacity to ~4.5× the 2024 level by 2028; the Sumitomo Densetsu deconsolidation (renamed Semlinks) in H1 FY3/2027; continued compression of cross-shareholdings and inventories (the FY3/2026 affiliate-share sale gain is the flip side of that programme). Capital returns: FY3/2027 dividend guide ¥44 post-split (¥176 pre-split equivalent), raised with Rev.2.

blocks.heading: 8. Other information
blocks.html:
Corporate actions: 4-for-1 stock split effective 1 July 2026 (register S6); Sumitomo Densetsu deconsolidated in H1 FY3/2027 (renamed Semlinks; −¥8.6bn H1 OP drag disclosed). The shares fell 6.98% on 16 November 2026 to ¥1,413 (post-split) despite the H1 beat and raise — secondary data put the price ~62% below its June 2026 split-adjusted high; the desk does not verify intraday narratives, but the de-rating frames the market's scepticism about H2 delivery and optical-cycle duration. Major shareholders are 未取得 in the sources used. Next results: Q3 FY3/2027, expected late January 2027.

Cash conversion is the counterweight to the profit story. In H1 FY3/2027 operating cash flow fell 44.7% year on year to ¥139.4bn despite record operating profit of ¥219.6bn, because inventories rose ¥201.7bn in the half to ¥1,219.8bn at end-September 2026. The full-year history shows why the level matters: inventories have risen every year since FY3/2017 (¥449,070mn) and reached ¥1,018,148mn at FY3/2026-end, while interest-bearing debt has fallen from its FY3/2023 peak of ¥891,680mn to ¥557,266mn — the balance sheet has been funding growth through working capital rather than debt. The mid-term plan's pre-tax ROIC target of at least 15% (company-reported pre-tax ROIC was 14.7% in FY3/2026) is the metric that this inventory trajectory has to reconcile with.

blocks.heading: 9. Basis of preparation
blocks.html: Sources: the PL/segment sheet for Sumitomo Electric (5802) in its CORRECTED form — the programme audit found the original main build had assigned FY3/2022–23 segment-note columns positionally in the wrong order (the tanshin's printed column order changed with the FY2024 documents); 48 cells were corrected in place on 17 November 2026 and re-audited to zero differences (register S15; rollout log fix-sei-segments). This report uses the corrected copy (MD5 96e7291f…) for all segment figures; headline IS/BS/CF figures are identical across copies. Main window FY3/2022–FY3/2026 plus the FY3/2017–FY3/2021 history block; register S1–S15. Also used: the guidance tracker (56-company edition, 17 November 2026) and the interview pack for 5802 (Q2 FY3/2027 tanshin and segment note, President's briefing slides and DC strategy deck, 12 November 2026 — slides only, no Q&A). Regional disclosure: none in the tanshin for the main window (register S4); history-block regions (FY3/2017–19, entity- and customer-location) are shown on their own basis only. The sheet's template 'Estimate' columns were not used. Calculated figures are labelled as such. Gaps （未取得 / not disclosed): regional sales and profit for FY3/2022–26; order intake and backlog (not disclosed as a group total); units, capacity (in fibre-km) and utilisation; R&D and employees in the tanshin; data-centre revenue in ¥ (not disclosed in any material read); the price/volume split of the optical profit; the copper pass-through lag; segment guidance beyond the Infocommunications OP forecast; the perimeter of the renamed 'Digital & AI' field vs the current segment; major shareholders. The share price is the 16 November 2026 close, post-split (StockAnalysis price history; StockInvest); market capitalisation is StockInvest's ¥4.41tn (calculated on 3,119.6mn post-split shares: ¥4.408tn — agrees). Rating and price target are 'Under Review' placeholders — no rating or target has been set by the analyst for this coverage, and nothing in this report is a forecast or a recommendation.
